itemUsage.en: Lumen, chapel caregiver of Gran Faro, here to soothe your wounds.
itemUsage.zh: 格兰法洛的礼拜堂护工流明，将会抚平你的伤痕。

itemDesc.en: Compared to his work with the Inquisition, he's more confident in tending to others after all.
itemDesc.zh: 相比于在审判庭的工作，他还是对照顾别人更有自信。

description.en: The next attack causes the target and nearby allies to receive healing equal to <@ba.vup>{aura.heal_scale:0%}</> of Lumen's ATK every second for <@ba.vup>{aura.projectile_life_time}</> seconds

description.en:
ATK <@ba.vup>+{atk:0%}</>, ASPD <@ba.vup>+{attack_speed}</>, prioritizes healing units with <$ba.debuff>negative statuses</>; ammo is consumed if the target has a <$ba.debuff>negative status</>, increasing healing to <@ba.vup>{heal_scale:0%}</> of ATK, and removing <$ba.debuff>negative statuses</> from the target. 
<@ba.rem>Attack has <@ba.vup>{attack@trigger_time}</> ammo. Skill ends when all ammo is used (can manually deactivate skill)</>
description.zh: 攻击力<@ba.vup>+{atk:0%}</>，攻击速度<@ba.vup>+{attack_speed}</>，优先治疗处于<$ba.debuff>异常状态</>中的单位；只在治疗<$ba.debuff>异常状态</>中的单位时会消耗子弹，使该次治疗量提升至攻击力的<@ba.vup>{heal_scale:0%}</>并解除目标所受的<$ba.debuff>异常状态</>\n<@ba.rem>攻击装有<@ba.vup>{attack@trigger_time}</>发子弹，打完后技能结束（期间可随时停止技能）</>

description.en: When an ally within range receives a negative status, heal them for 80% of Lumen's ATK. 12 seconds cooldown.

description.zh: 攻击范围内的友方受到异常状态时，立刻治疗目标相当于流明攻击力80%的生命，该效果有10<@ba.talpu>（-2）</>秒冷却时间

Operator Lumen has demonstrated a remarkable aptitude for wide-range healing in tandem with endowment of effects of benefit upon Operators.

This badge is hereby conferred upon the above named.

description.en:
On Jordi's lower leg is an already almost indiscernible scar, left when he was nine years old.
Young Jordi always loved to sit on the benches that lined the town plaza, hugging his knees, spacing out as he stared at the lighthouse statue in the plaza's center. Whenever he did, he did so for the whole day. Jordi had carefully chosen his position, and watching from this angle at sunset, the sinking sun in the west would line up with the tip of the lighthouse for the briefest moment, like this tiny little lighthouse too had come alight.
Regrettably, it was a fleeting scene, and in the span of a few short breaths, the lighthouse statue would once again go out. Everything about it would be rapidly shrouded in shadow, engulfed by darkness. What he had just witnessed was much like an illusion, gone without a trace.
Fortunately, the sun would rise as it did before the next day, and the lighthouse would come alight again. Just for a moment, of course.
On the day of his ninth birthday, Jordi decided to do something big. He wanted to grab hold of something more lasting. He'd try and see for himself what the town's elder workers were so proud of yet kept so secret, see for himself the colossal structure the parents he'd never met had disappeared in, see for himself that true 'Eye of Iberia.' Jordi began to climb the statue in the plaza, believing as long as he stood on its top, he'd be able to see the true rays of the lighthouse piercing through the fog. He clambered inch by inch, hearing the passersby in the plaza shrieking frantically, but the top was right there before him, he just had to make one final leap...
Jordi suddenly felt himself falling—the protrusion he'd used as footing likely crumbled—but why he was falling was no longer important. Jordi had struggled so he could cast his sight far away. Even if it was only for a split-second, he wanted to see it.
Nothing. There was nothing. The fog was like a gauze, covering all upon the surface of the sea.
When Jordi came to, he was already back at home, his leg bandaged, the scent of meat porridge pervading the room. Hearing the sound of Jordi turning over, Thiago poked his body out of the kitchen. Jordi thought he'd be in for a ferocious scolding, but Thiago simply stared at him for a moment, let out a sigh, and pointed in the direction of the desk. There was laid a spyglass, glittering in alluring bronze.
That was a bygone affair, years and years ago, and now the scar has even faded. Only the small town's plaza seems to have been overlooked by time, resting unchanged. Jordi sits in his younger self's most favorite spot. Now he's seen the true Eye of Iberia, yet he can no longer sit on this bench with his uncle, listening to those heart-racing stories, taking turns at the spyglass through which they'd gaze far away.
But even with the help of a spyglass, they still couldn't see anything. It was the one thing the two of them silently, tacitly, never mentioned to each other.
description.zh:
乔迪的小腿上有一道已经几乎无法辨识的疤痕，那是他九岁的时候留下的。
小时候的乔迪，总喜欢坐在镇子广场边的长椅上，抱着膝盖，只是呆呆看着广场中心的那座灯塔雕像，一待就是一整天。乔迪精心选择过他的位置，从这个角度望去，每到日落时分，在某个短暂的瞬间，西沉的太阳会与雕像顶端重合，如同这座小小的灯塔也亮起了灯光。
遗憾的是，这景象稍纵即逝，仅仅几次呼吸之后，灯塔雕像就会再度熄灭，周围的一切快速被阴影所笼罩，被黑暗所吞没。刚才的所见如同一场幻觉，消失无踪。
好在，第二天太阳依旧会升起，灯塔依旧会点亮，当然，还是只有一瞬间。
在九岁生日的那天，乔迪决定干一件大事，他终究还是想要抓住更加恒久的事物，他试图亲眼看看镇子上的老工人们为之自豪却又讳莫如深的东西，亲眼看看未曾谋面的父母消失于其中的巨构，亲眼看看那座真正的“伊比利亚之眼”。乔迪开始攀登广场雕像，他相信只要站在雕像顶端，就一定能看到真正的灯塔那穿破浓雾的光芒。一尺接着一尺，他听到广场上的路人们在慌张地尖叫，但雕像的顶端就在眼前，只要最终轻轻一跃……
乔迪突然感觉到自己在下坠，大概是本来踏足的凸起处崩解了，但如今原因已经不再重要。乔迪努力向远方投出自己的目光，哪怕只是短短一瞥也好，他想要看见。
没有，什么都没有。雾气像一层薄纱，覆盖了海面上的一切。
乔迪再次醒来的时候已经是在自己家中，腿上被打了绷带，肉粥的香味弥漫在房间里。听到乔迪翻身的声音，蒂亚戈从厨房中探出身子。乔迪本以为会狠狠挨上一顿骂，可蒂亚戈只是定定地看了他一会儿，叹了口气，指了指书桌的方向。那里放着一支单筒望远镜，闪耀着迷人的黄铜色泽。
那已经是很多年前的事情了，如今就连疤痕都已经褪色，唯有小镇广场似乎被时间遗忘，永恒不变。乔迪坐在小时候最喜欢的位置上，他如今已经见过了真正的伊比利亚之眼，却再也没办法和自己的叔叔坐在长椅上，听着那些激动人心的故事，轮流举着望远镜看向远方了。
然而就算借助望远镜，依然什么都看不见。唯有此事，两人默契地从未向对方提及。

description.en: To the Inquisition has come an Ægir. I can assure you, not for the past thirty years... no, forty, at the very least! Has an Ægir set foot in the Inquisition's court in any capacity other than that of the tried. The very words themselves are preposterous. It was a young man, not particularly remarkable at first glance. Of fair height, but didn't stand too straight or firm. His features were proper, but lacked any good presence. In all regards, not someone especially worth minding. If it weren't for the fact he was an Ægir, I think even someone new like myself wouldn't have batted an eye at him, with how unassuming and overt his arrival was. But now, all the Inquisition is abound with the rumor of this Ægir. Some say he's some wicked convict's bosom friend, merely held temporarily in custody, but this young man—before I forget, his name is Jordi Fontanarossa—clearly has no restrictions placed on his movements. Others believe he's a signal from Lord Carmen that the Inquisition is once again to admit and even promote some of the Islanders in due time. However, Jordi Fontanarossa himself is feeble and weak, and his education lacking. At best, he would be capable of some meager secretarial work, and it doesn't seem as if his position is particularly lofty. Given our workplaces are so near each other, I've had the opportunity to observe him. This Ægir punches in at twenty minutes before his shift each morning, sometimes a little later, but he's never tardy. He's prone to occasional clumsiness; he once caused a misprint of documents after poorly operating the press, wasting quires of business paper. If I hadn't chanced to pass by and stop the machine, who knows how his accident could have evolved. I wasn't going out of my way to help him, of course, simply taking responsibility for our work. And no matter how I explained to him as such, the Ægir just persisted with his smile. He'd clearly misunderstood something! Such a loathsome smile! One time, in relation to a vital operation, some colleagues and I were working overtime into the night. The Ægir brought a bucket of drinks over, telling us it was some herbal tea he'd mixed himself. I wasn't interested in having any, but that sort of thing is effective at keeping one awake, so for the sake of work, it would have to do. It was about early morning by the time we were done with overtime, and everyone was audibly starving, running on bellies filled with nothing but tea. There in the dark, I suddenly heard footsteps approach, then saw someone had lit a lantern. It was that Ægir, who himself hadn't left for some reason, and had a pot in his hands too, with several bags clearly filled with food hanging from his wrists. 'Ah, are you all done with work? You must be exhausted.' The man seemed all too apologetic as he regarded us. 'I'm sorry I couldn't be of help with any of it. All I could do was make some food that'd be light on the stomach...' With no patience for hearing out his habitual self-debasement and humbling excuses, I took his pot without any fanfare. It was a vanilla porridge, and all signs pointed to it being yet another recipe beneficial to health. Lord Carmen having taken in this Ægir as a disciple? Absolutely never would I lend credence to such a ridiculous rumor. That said, based on what I've seen, should the Inquisition decide it would readmit Islanders, I suppose it would hardly be a bad thing.
description.zh:
审判庭来了一个阿戈尔人。
我可以保证，往前数至少三十年……不，四十年！都没有任何一个阿戈尔人曾以受审以外的身份踏足过审判庭，这听起来就很荒唐。
那是一个看不出有什么特别之处的年轻人。个头尚可，但身形不算挺拔。面容算得上端正，但没什么气势。不管怎么看都不是什么特别值得关注的人物。如果不是因为他是一个阿戈尔人，还如此堂而皇之地出现在审判庭，恐怕连我这样的新人也不会特地多看他一眼。
但现在整个审判庭内，四处都充斥着与这个阿戈尔人相关的流言。
有人说他是某个邪恶罪犯的相关者，只是被暂时拘押在此。可这个年轻人——对了，他叫乔迪·方塔纳罗萨——分明没有受到任何行动上的限制。也有人认为这是卡门阁下释放的某种信号，审判庭接下来将要重新接纳甚至重用一部分岛民。但乔迪·方塔纳罗萨瘦弱无力，学识平平，平时只能做点文书工作，看起来也不像是得到了重用的样子。
因为工作场所距离很近，所以我有机会对其展开观察。
这个阿戈尔人每天早晨会在上班前二十分钟准时打卡，有时候稍微迟一点，不过不会真的迟到。他偶尔有点笨手笨脚，曾经误操作机器导致文件印刷出错，浪费了几十张公务用纸。如果不是我路过停下机器，谁知道他还会出什么岔子。
我当然不是特地帮他，只是出于对工作负责的态度。尽管我这么解释了，但那个阿戈尔人却还是一直笑，他明显误会了什么，真是讨厌的笑容！
有一次，涉及一场重要行动，我和其他同僚集体加班到深夜。阿戈尔人提了一桶饮料过来，说是自己调配的什么花草茶。本来我是不想喝的，但这东西在提神方面确实有效，为了工作，也顾不上其他的了。
我们加完班时，已经差不多是凌晨，大家饥肠辘辘，肚子里除了茶水外什么都没有。黑暗中，我忽然听到有一个脚步声由远及近，然后就看到有人点亮了一盏小灯。是那个阿戈尔人，他竟然也还没走，手里还端着一个小锅，手腕上挂着几个明显是装了食物的袋子。
“啊，大家已经结束工作了吗？真是辛苦了。”
这个家伙好像很抱歉似的看着我们，“对不起，各位的工作我帮不上什么忙，只能准备一点对胃负担不重的食物……”
我懒得听他习惯性地自我贬低和自谦的那套说辞，直接动手把锅接过来。
里面是一锅香草粥，恐怕又是什么对健康有益的配方。
说什么卡门阁下已将这名阿戈尔人收为弟子，这种荒谬的传闻我是绝对不会信的。不过，如果审判庭真的决定重新接纳岛民，依我所见，这倒并不是一件坏事。
